title: Light and air
subtitle: Photoperiod, oxygen and airflow
description: Light switches the seedling from stretching to building, so darkness and photoperiod change its shape the most. Oxygen partial pressure, not total pressure, sets how fast germination happens. And airflow past the seed matters little, because the seed coat and the tissue limit how much oxygen gets in.

scenes.title: Light and air
lines: Three things flight hardware controls: the light schedule, the atmosphere, and the air moving past the seed.
Light intensity is not modelled here, only darkness and the photoperiod.

captions.text: In darkness the seedling stretches its hypocotyl and keeps its hook closed. Light stops the stretching and opens the hook: de-etiolation.

With ordinary air at that pressure ({C.env.po2_kpa|1} kPa of oxygen) it slips to {C.endosperm_rupture_h|1} h, and at {D.env.po2_kpa|1} kPa to {D.endosperm_rupture_h|1} h. What matters is the oxygen partial pressure.

scenes.title: Airflow past the seed, in microgravity

captions.text: In microgravity warm air does not rise, so only fans move air past the seed. Here the air speed is the only difference.

The fan raises mass transfer through the air (Sherwood number {A.sherwood:max|1} to {C.sherwood:max|1}), yet at {A.t@30|0} h the radicle tip sits at {A.o2_tip_kpa@30|1} versus {C.o2_tip_kpa@30|1} kPa of oxygen, and the core of the axis at {A.o2_core_min_kpa@30|1} and {C.o2_core_min_kpa@30|1} kPa.
The seed coat and the respiring tissue limit the oxygen supply, not the air around the seed.
